text:
maria_sales: Quick one — medtech prospect asking if we can guarantee low tail latency for a trial that will route traffic from Canada and Brazil. they want a short window (2 weeks) with 95th percentile < 200ms and a list of any third-party subprocessors touching data.

luis_tech: Do we have region capacity for Canada (toronto) + brazil (sa-east1) for bursty traffic? they expect spikes from scheduled scans.

samir_sre: Toronto yes on hosted, SA-East1 limited — we have edge pools but would need dedicated burst or cross-region fallback.

maria_sales: Customer insists no cross-border storage; they said "no egress outside country" in the security questionnaire. is that a hard blocker?

anya_security: Flagging PHI concerns — medtech. if they require no cross-border storage we need Private with on-prem or customer VPC + control plane options. Hosted cannot promise zero cross-border unless pinned in a dedicated deployment.

luis_tech: For a 2-week trial we could offer a short-lived Dedicated reservation in toronto and a candidate in sa-east1, or configure tenant affinity to local edge with strict route policy. Need pricing for temporary reserved capacity.

maria_sales: Pricing ask — how to price a 2-week dedicated burst vs hosted per-token? they want a ballpark now to decide.

samir_sre: Rough: small GPU pool (2x A10G equiv) for 2 weeks ~ $Xk/week + setup; hosted per-token might be cheaper but can't meet the 'no egress' constraint. I can run exact calc if ops_ashley confirms infra quotas.

ops_ashley: I can check quota and give numbers by EOD. also need to know model size + expected qps and sequence length.

maria_sales: Model: ~7B, avg seq 512, peak qps ~40 for 30min job windows.

luis_tech: With those numbers continuous batching should help. config example to pin tenant in toronto:```json
{
  "routing": {
    "preferred_region": "ca-central1",
    "failover": "no-cross-border",
    "subprocessor_whitelist": ["redwood-core","kms-provider-ca"]
  },
  "capacity": {
    "gpus": 2,
    "type": "a10g",
    "duration": "2w"
  }
}```

anya_security: Also need full subprocessor manifest and SOC2 report. I'll attach the medtech-specific sec-qa and ask legal on acceptable attestation.

maria_sales: I uploaded customer sec questionnaire (sec_q_medtech.pdf) to the deal thread. they also request a list of physical location auditors for sa-east1 — is that something infra can provide?

samir_sre: We can provide cloud provider's subprocessor list + our subprocessors. For on-prem/private we'd pass through only the customer's infra, so fewer subprocessors. For hosted we'll enumerate: cloud infra, logging vendor, kms provider (if BYOK not used).

luis_tech: Question for security — if customer permits BYOK with KMS in-country (Canada/Brazil), can hosted meet the no-storage-cross-border ask?

anya_security: BYOK helps with keys but not with metadata/replication. If the customer requires all data residency (no copy outside country) we still need dedicated or private. BYOK reduces risk but isn't sufficient alone.

maria_sales: Anything else I should tell the customer now to keep momentum? they asked for an informal timeline and blocker list.

ops_ashley: Timeline: confirm infra quota (today), pricing estimate (tomorrow morning), security attestation + subproc list (security to provide EOD), setup of temporary Dedicated (if approved) ~48-72 hrs. Blockers: legal signoff on subproc list + funding for short-term reserve.

luis_tech: I'll prepare a short tech note on latency expectations and fallback behavior to share.

anya_security: I'll post the initial subproc manifest and the PHI-specific checklist here when ready.

maria_sales: Perfect — I'll update customer: propose temporary Dedicated in Canada, optionally Brazil edge; explain BYOK isn't a full solution; give timeline. thanks all :thumbsup:
